scheme_name: Scheme for Supply of Improved Seeds for Fodder
description:
The Scheme for Supply of Improved Seeds for Fodder was launched by the Government of India in the year 2014. 

This scheme aims to enhance the availability of quality fodder seeds to farmers across the country. 

The initiative is particularly crucial given the significant role of livestock in the Indian economy. 

Livestock contributes approximately 4.11% to the Gross Value Added in agriculture. 

The scheme is implemented under the National Livestock Mission. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the productivity of livestock by ensuring that farmers have access to high-quality fodder. 

The government aims to increase the availability of improved fodder seeds by 20% by the year 2025. 

The scheme also targets to increase the area under fodder cultivation by at least 10% annually. 

Farmers are provided with improved varieties of fodder seeds at subsidized rates. 

The subsidy provided under this scheme is up to 50% of the cost of seeds. 

The maximum subsidy amount can reach up to INR 1,500 per quintal of seeds. 

This financial assistance is designed to make quality seeds more accessible to farmers. 

The scheme focuses on various types of fodder crops including legumes and grasses. 

Some of the improved varieties promoted under this scheme include Napier grass, Lucerne, and Cowpea. 

Farmers can benefit from the scheme by cultivating these improved varieties which have higher nutritional value. 

The nutritional content of improved fodder can lead to better milk production and overall livestock health. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily targeted at farmers engaged in livestock rearing. 

Farmers must possess a valid landholding to qualify for the subsidy. 

There are no specific age limits set for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, farmers must demonstrate an active engagement in livestock farming. 

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability. 

Farmers must first approach the local Agricultural Department office. 

They need to fill out an application form that includes details about their landholding and livestock. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership, identity proof, and a declaration of livestock ownership. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the concerned authorities. 

The verification process typically takes about 15 days. 

Upon successful verification, farmers receive a subsidy approval. 

Farmers can then purchase the seeds from designated suppliers or government nurseries. 

The seeds are available at subsidized rates which are significantly lower than the market price. 

The scheme is operational throughout the year. 

However, farmers are encouraged to apply during the pre-sowing season to ensure timely availability of seeds. 

The disbursement of subsidies is generally processed within 30 days of seed purchase. 

The implementing authorities for this scheme include the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying oversees the overall functioning of the scheme. 

Farmers can contact the local Animal Husbandry office for any queries related to the scheme. 

The contact details of the local offices can be found on the official website of the Ministry. 

The scheme also aims to promote awareness about the importance of fodder cultivation. 

Workshops and training programs are organized for farmers to educate them about improved fodder practices. 

The government has set a target to train at least 100,000 farmers annually under this scheme. 

By 2025, the government aims to achieve a 30% increase in the number of farmers adopting improved fodder cultivation practices. 

The scheme has been instrumental in improving the livelihoods of farmers engaged in dairy and livestock farming. 

In the year 2022, approximately 200,000 quintals of improved fodder seeds were distributed under this scheme. 

The scheme has also contributed to an increase in milk production by an estimated 10% in regions where it has been implemented. 

Farmers have reported an increase in milk yield from 5 liters to 7 liters per day after switching to improved fodder. 

This increase in productivity translates to higher incomes for farmers. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2023-2024. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted regularly to assess its impact. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to improve the scheme and address any challenges faced. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance the overall productivity of the livestock sector in India. 

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by the year 2022. 

The initiative also contributes to food security by ensuring that livestock are well-fed and healthy. 

Healthy livestock are essential for sustainable agricultural practices and rural development. 

The scheme is expected to play a vital role in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals related to poverty alleviation and hunger. 

In summary, the Scheme for Supply of Improved Seeds for Fodder is a comprehensive initiative aimed at improving fodder availability for livestock farmers in India. 

With specific objectives and measurable targets, the scheme is designed to enhance productivity and support the livelihoods of farmers. 

Through financial assistance and educational programs, the government is working towards a more sustainable and productive livestock sector. 

Farmers are encouraged to actively participate in the scheme to reap its benefits. 

The scheme not only supports individual farmers but also contributes to the overall growth of the agricultural economy in India.
